finding: Broker release/conflict resolution can leave multiple opposing reservation artifacts for the same shared path without a supersession or last-writer contract, so `resolve` may report ready while later close/preclose sees the conflict again.
expectedBehavior: Reservation resolution artifacts should have a formal supersession interface with a single authoritative release order per conflict set, or close should consume a deterministic latest valid artifact and explain why older artifacts are ignored.
evidenceOrRepro: Current implementation and focused regression are green. `collectResolutionAuthorizedForeignTaskIds` groups artifacts by normalized participants and shared paths, validates broker authority, and ignores an older opposing artifact when a newer valid release order exists. `broker-conflict-supersession.test.ts` proves the older authority cannot authorize TASK-A while the newer authority authorizes only TASK-B; `npx tsc --noEmit` and `git diff --check` also exit 0.
followUp: Keep opposing-artifact selection deterministic by createdAt plus resolutionId and retain fail-closed behavior for malformed, stale, or unauthorized artifacts.
